plain_text:
The only way to find out whether you have a blood clot is to get
medical help. If you know the warning signs, you're more likely to
recognize them and get help as soon as possible.
semantic_text: The only way to find out whether you have a blood clot is to get medical help. If you know the warning signs, you're more likely to recognize them and get help as soon as possible.

plain_text:
Blood clots can affect anyone, but some factors can increase
your risk. They include:
semantic_text: Blood clots can affect anyone, but some factors can increase your risk. They include:

plain_text:
■ Age. Clots can occur at any age, but people older than
60 are at greatest risk.
■ Family history. If your family has a history of clots or
clotting disorders, you are more likely to develop them.
■ Lack of movement. Sitting or lying down for a long time
(for example, during a long flight or extended hospital stay)
reduces blood flow, which increases your risk of clots.
■ Pregnancy and childbirth. Blood is more likely to clot
during pregnancy, making pregnant people more susceptible.
This risk can last through the first six weeks after the
baby is born.
■ Certain health conditions. These include cancer (and
cancer treatment), heart disease, diabetes, blood disorders,
certain autoimmune conditions, and COVID-19.
■ Certain medications. Some medications can slow blood
flow and cause clotting. These include drugs that affect the
hormone estrogen (such as birth control pills).
■ Smoking. Smoking damages blood vessels and makes it
more difficult for blood to clot properly.

plain_text:
If you have multiple risk factors, you're even more likely to
develop blood clots.
semantic_text: If you have multiple risk factors, you're even more likely to develop blood clots.

plain_text:
If your health care provider suspects that you may have a blood
clot, they will ask you about your symptoms and medical history
and perform a physical exam.
semantic_text: If your health care provider suspects that you may have a blood clot, they will ask you about your symptoms and medical history and perform a physical exam.

plain_text: To learn about your medical history, they may ask about:
semantic_text: To learn about your medical history, they may ask about:

plain_text:
■ Your overall health
■ Any prescription medicines you're taking
■ Any recent surgeries or injuries you've had
■ Whether you've been treated for cancer
semantic_text: ■ Your overall health ■ Any prescription medicines you're taking ■ Any recent surgeries or injuries you've had ■ Whether you've been treated for cancer

plain_text: During the physical exam, they will:
semantic_text: During the physical exam, they will:

plain_text:
■ Check for signs of blood clots
■ Check your blood pressure, your heart, and your lungs
semantic_text: ■ Check for signs of blood clots ■ Check your blood pressure, your heart, and your lungs

plain_text:
They may also order tests such as a blood test or an imaging test
to diagnose a clot or a clotting disorder. These can include:
semantic_text: They may also order tests such as a blood test or an imaging test to diagnose a clot or a clotting disorder. These can include:

plain_text:
■ Ultrasound. This is the most common test for diagnosing
blood clots in the arms and legs. Ultrasound uses sound
waves to create pictures of blood flowing through the arteries
and veins.
■ D-dimer test. This blood test measures a substance in the
blood that's released when a blood clot dissolves. If the test
shows high levels of this substance, you may have a clotting
disorder.
■ Other tests. If the doctor suspects a clot in the lungs, they
may order additional imaging tests to confirm the diagnosis.
These tests provide detailed images of the lungs and can help
pinpoint the location of a blood clot.

These tests provide detailed images of the lungs and can help pinpoint the location of a blood clot.

plain_text:
Blood thinners are the most common treatment for blood clots.
These medications help prevent new clots from forming and
keep existing clots from getting bigger. However, they can't break
up clots that have already formed.
semantic_text: Blood thinners are the most common treatment for blood clots. These medications help prevent new clots from forming and keep existing clots from getting bigger. However, they can't break up clots that have already formed.

plain_text:
In some cases, doctors may use clot-dissolving medications to
break up clots that have already formed. Very rarely, surgery may
be necessary to remove a blood clot. These treatments are less
common and depend on the type of clot, its severity, and where
it's located.
semantic_text: In some cases, doctors may use clot-dissolving medications to break up clots that have already formed. Very rarely, surgery may be necessary to remove a blood clot. These treatments are less common and depend on the type of clot, its severity, and where it's located.

plain_text:
If you have a blood clot, it is important to work with your
doctor to develop a treatment plan that is right for you.
semantic_text: If you have a blood clot, it is important to work with your doctor to develop a treatment plan that is right for you.

plain_text:
Stay active. Exercise keeps your blood flowing, which
makes it harder for clots to develop.
semantic_text: Stay active. Exercise keeps your blood flowing, which makes it harder for clots to develop.

plain_text:
Take movement breaks. It's important to move your
body regularly, especially during long trips or extended
periods of sitting. If you can, get up and move around
every 2 to 3 hours.
semantic_text: Take movement breaks. It's important to move your body regularly, especially during long trips or extended periods of sitting. If you can, get up and move around every 2 to 3 hours.

plain_text:
Stay hydrated. Drink plenty of fluid to keep your
blood flowing.
semantic_text: Stay hydrated. Drink plenty of fluid to keep your blood flowing.

plain_text:
Say no to smoking. Kicking the habit is a win-win for
your overall health. And if you don't smoke, don't start!
semantic_text: Say no to smoking. Kicking the habit is a win-win for your overall health. And if you don't smoke, don't start!

plain_text:
Maintain a healthy weight. Excess body weight can
increase your risk of blood clots. If you're concerned
about how your weight might affect your risk for blood
clots, talk to your doctor about safe and effective weight
management strategies.
semantic_text: Maintain a healthy weight. Excess body weight can increase your risk of blood clots. If you're concerned about how your weight might affect your risk for blood clots, talk to your doctor about safe and effective weight management strategies.

plain_text:
Follow the doctor's orders. If your doctor prescribes
blood thinners, follow their instructions closely.
semantic_text: Follow the doctor's orders. If your doctor prescribes blood thinners, follow their instructions closely.

plain_text:
Try compression stockings. Your doctor may
recommend these to improve blood flow in your
legs and arms.
semantic_text: Try compression stockings. Your doctor may recommend these to improve blood flow in your legs and arms.
